title: False Personation (Pen. Code, § 529(a))

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: The defendant is charged [in Count ______] with falsely impersonating another person in that person’s private or official capacity and performing certain acts [in violation of Penal Code section 529(a)].
To prove that the defendant is guilty of this crime, the People must prove that:
1. The defendant falsely impersonated another person in the other person’s private or official capacity;
2. While falsely impersonating that person, the defendant:
2. [A. Posted bail or acted as surety for anyone in any proceeding, before any judge or officer authorized to take that bail or surety(;/.)]
2. [B(1). Verified, published, acknowledged, or proved, in the name of that person, any written document;
2. B(2). When the defendant did so, (he/she) intended that the written document be recorded, delivered, or used as though it were an authentic document(./;)]

2. [C. Did any act that, if done by the person being falsely impersonated, might cause (that person to be liable in a lawsuit or criminal prosecution/[or] that person to pay any amount of money/[or] that person to be subject to any charge, forfeiture, or penalty/[or] the defendant or anyone else to receive a benefit as a result).]

bench_notes.text: The court has a sua sponte duty to give this instruction defining the elements of the crime.

authority.text: • Elements. Pen. Code, § 529(a). • Additional Act Requirement *People v. Guion* (2013) 213 Cal.App.4th 1426, 1431–1432 [153 Cal.Rptr.3d 395].

related_issues.text: Penal Code section 529(a)(3) does not require any specific mental state beyond intentionally falsely impersonating another. *People v. Rathert* (2000) 24 Cal.4th 200, 205–206 [99 Cal.Rptr.2d 779, 6 P.3d 700].
